claims.claim: MP Materials occupies a strategic chain from rare-earth ore through separated NdPr to magnets used in motors and defense/industrial systems, linking domestic resource processing to electrification, automation and national supply resilience.

Vertical integration can reduce dependence on foreign processing/magnet supply, but successor bottlenecks move to separation yield, magnet commissioning, customer qualification, scale utilization and economically durable offtake.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Domestic mine-to-separated-product-to-magnet capability addresses multiple stages of a concentrated rare-earth supply chain.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Domestic downstream conversion can diversify strategic magnet supply if ramp and qualification succeed.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Strategic demand is broad, while economics remain sensitive to ramp execution, policy support and rare-earth pricing.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: NdFeB magnets are performance-critical in many applications, but motor redesign, recycling and alternative magnet chemistries can reduce intensity in some uses.

risks.risk: Commissioning, qualification and utilization can become binding constraints after upstream resource availability is solved.

causalEdges.mechanism: motors and strategic systems require compact high-strength magnetic materials
causalEdges.falsifier: alternative motor/magnet designs materially reduce NdFeB intensity across major end uses

causalEdges.mechanism: domestic processing and magnet capacity reduce reliance on concentrated foreign conversion stages
causalEdges.falsifier: ramp, qualification or cost failures prevent competitive domestic volume

unknowns.unknown: Long-run standalone economics without government support and realized utilization of new capacity remain unknown.

claims.claim: Current downstream progress strengthens execution credibility, but government price protection and strategic commitments mean observed economics should not be treated as proof of fully market-clearing standalone returns.

Simultaneous expansion across separation and magnet capacity creates correlated construction, commissioning, qualification and capital-allocation risk; strategic importance does not eliminate those operating constraints.

factors.name: policyDependence
factors.basis: Government support can de-risk strategic capacity while obscuring unsupported market economics.

factors.name: executionConcentration
factors.basis: Multiple large ramp programs create correlated schedule and qualification exposure.

factors.name: confidenceInflation
factors.basis: Commercial milestones are real, but future 10X utilization and economics are not yet achieved facts.

risks.risk: Policy/contract support may be necessary for economics that are not yet demonstrated on a fully standalone basis.
Construction, commissioning and customer qualification delays can strand or underutilize capital.
Competitive response, recycling or alternative motor designs can reduce expected rare-earth intensity over time.

causalEdges.mechanism: price floors/commitments can stabilize investment returns during domestic scale-up
causalEdges.falsifier: new capacity demonstrates durable competitive economics after support rolls off or becomes non-material

contradictions.claim: Strategic supply-chain value versus policy-supported economics
contradictions.resolution: Both can be true; resilience value may justify support while standalone commercial durability remains an open economic question.

unknowns.unknown: Exact unsupported long-run unit economics and realized 10X utilization are not established by current evidence.
